question: A 61-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a constant, dull headache and generalized body pains for the past 8 months. She has also had difficulty hearing from her left side, which started a month after the onset of the headaches. Five months ago, she had surgery to correct a fracture of the right femur that occurred without a fall or any significant trauma. Five years ago, she underwent a total thyroidectomy for localized thyroid carcinoma. She takes levothyroxine and calcium supplements, which she started after menopause. Physical examination reveals a prominent forehead and irregular, tender skull surface. Bony tenderness is present over bilateral hip and knee joints, with decreased range of motion of the right hip joint and increased anterior curvature of both tibias. Laboratory studies show a highly elevated level of alkaline phosphatase, with vitamin D, calcium and PTH levels within normal limits. A plain x-ray of the head is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Lytic lesions with no sclerotic margin
options.opb: Multiple, well-defined, punched out lytic lesions
options.opd: Periosteal trabeculations with radiolucent marrow hyperplasia

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "61-year-old woman with constant dull headache" -> "headache and body pains for 8 months" -> "difficulty hearing from left side" -> "surgery for right femur fracture without trauma" -> "history of total thyroidectomy for carcinoma" -> "elevated alkaline phosphatase levels" -> "prominent forehead and irregular skull surface" -> "bony tenderness over hip and knee joints" -> "decreased range of motion in right hip" -> "increased anterior curvature of tibias" -> "likely indicates Paget's disease" -> "plain x-ray shows mixed lytic and sclerotic lesions" -> 85%

CHAIN: "61-year-old woman with chronic symptoms" -> "constant dull headache and body pains" -> "hearing loss on left side" -> "surgery for right femur fracture" -> "previous thyroid carcinoma treatment" -> "high alkaline phosphatase suggests bone metabolism issue" -> "physical exam shows irregular skull and bony tenderness" -> "features consistent with Paget's disease" -> "x-ray findings typically include mixed lytic and sclerotic lesions" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with chronic headache and body pain" -> "hearing difficulty on left side" -> "surgical history of femur fracture" -> "thyroid cancer treatment history" -> "elevated alkaline phosphatase indicates bone pathology" -> "physical exam reveals skull irregularities and bony tenderness" -> "symptoms suggestive of Paget's disease" -> "x-ray likely shows mixed lytic and sclerotic lesions" -> 80%

CHAIN: "61-year-old woman with persistent headache" -> "generalized body pains for 8 months" -> "hearing loss developed after headaches" -> "surgery for right femur fracture" -> "total thyroidectomy history" -> "high alkaline phosphatase levels" -> "prominent forehead and irregular skull" -> "bony tenderness in joints" -> "decreased hip motion and tibial curvature" -> "indicates possible Paget's disease" -> "x-ray findings may show mixed lytic and sclerotic lesions" -> 75%
analysis: The clinical presentation of the patient suggests Paget's disease of bone, characterized by elevated alkaline phosphatase levels, bone pain, and deformities such as the prominent forehead and anterior curvature of the tibias. In Paget's disease, radiographic findings typically include mixed lytic and sclerotic lesions due to the disorganized bone remodeling process. Therefore, the most likely x-ray finding in this case would be mixed lytic and sclerotic lesions, which aligns with option 'opc'.
